topic: A support network of 3 neighbours: preparedness for someone who needs help

content.hook: Who would check on you in a blackout?

slides.title: Who would *check on you* in a blackout?
slides.body: Build a support network of 3 neighbours. One evening is enough.

slides.title: Pick *3 neighbours*
slides.body: One next door, one nearby, one who is often home. Swap names and numbers on paper.

slides.title: Agree what *help* means
slides.body: A knock, a check-in, shared water or charging. Pick a simple door signal.

content.caption:
Neighbour support network for a power outage: who would check on you, and who would you check on?

Official guidance often points to the same idea. In the first hours of a crisis, the people closest to you are the first help available.

A simple start:
• Pick 3 neighbours: next door, nearby, and one who is often home.
• Swap names and phone numbers on paper, not just in your phone.
• Agree what help looks like: a knock on the door, a check-in, sharing water or a charger.
• Choose a simple signal, like a note on the door.
• Share only what you're comfortable with.

This matters most for older adults, wheelchair users and anyone who may need a hand.
